set.plain: Drug checking, prescribed benzos and stricter rules have all been tried for people who use benzos, but none has been tested in a way that shows whether it lowers harm. The review's authors call drug checking's results consistently positive, but those results are mostly about what tests detected and what people said they did afterwards. At one checking service, infrared testing found alprazolam, the drug in Xanax, in about 1 in 4 samples people thought were Xanax, and some testing methods often missed 'designer' benzos.

set.plain: In a 2018 survey at 27 harm reduction sites in British Columbia, Canada, about 3 in 4 people had used drugs alone at least once in the past week. The reason chosen most often was that using at home is easier and more comfortable; others did not want people to know or felt safer alone, and some wrote that they had no one to use with. The survey could not show whether using alone changes the risk of overdose, but coroners' reports it cites found that about 7 in 10 people who died of an overdose in the province in 2016 and 2017 were using alone.

set.plain: In one lab trial, 18 healthy adults who had not used cannabis for at least a month ate brownies with THC alone or with the same THC plus a large amount of CBD. With CBD, blood THC was higher, and people felt the drug more, felt sicker, had more trouble with memory and simple tasks, and had a faster heartbeat, without liking it more. Other test medicines, including a sedative, were given in every session, so it is not certain what caused the difference, and only one amount of CBD, eaten in a brownie, was tested.
